title: Cross-host Linux and macOS effect evidence
description: Objective: collect production-surface effect conformance evidence on actual Linux and macOS hosts for every frozen platform boundary, bound to one exact source commit and distribution. Deliverable: host-native fault schedules/evidence receipts and a reproducible cross-host aggregation protocol. NOT in scope: implementing platform classifiers, running off-host fixtures as proof, or weakening Windows behavior. Hard dependencies: Linux boundary task-f01ef545b1554a2cb5df340ce78f6a5c, macOS boundary task-45d12ecfa6ae4938b23af28fe7876a44, doctor task-1cafc7f9fcdc4c9299860b6b1e38275d, and distribution packaging task-739879d0d1ce4a7ea4d1430688cdc4dc. Measured at HEAD 30458af on win32: tests/fault/linux/** and tests/fault/macos/** are absent; archived tasks-e87a735386f643fe92c0eeff09bc4275/e94b2055e281489ea9e97820919f6856 have no landing commits, and their reopen notes explicitly require live Linux/macOS hosts. Consumer: task-22cfca91c5134b24aaf3e5734444fb93. Owned paths: tests/fault/linux/**, tests/fault/macos/**, cross-host evidence manifests/aggregation, and CI/host runner configuration only where approved.
definitionOfDone: On an actual Linux host and an actual macOS host, every hand-written PLATFORM_BOUNDARIES member runs crash-before/after activation and cancellation schedules against the production classifier/runner surface; each schedule asserts exact PROVEN/UNKNOWN code, layer, boundary, and a nonzero case count.

Each host record binds source commit, distribution manifest/digest, OS/kernel/arch, Node/pnpm/provider runtime closure, fixture/fault schedule digests, timestamps, and raw run receipts; unverifiable or mismatched bindings yield UNKNOWN and never PASS.
Linux and macOS receipts are canonical, immutable, independently verifiable, and aggregated without trusting caller-selected host claims; missing host evidence leaves only that OS row UNKNOWN.
No off-host test fixture, emulation label, or design claim is accepted as host proof; Windows stays a separate observation and is not weakened.
Host-native fault gates and the cross-host verifier exit 0, and task-22cfca91c5134b24aaf3e5734444fb93 is recorded as the acceptance consumer.
taskRails: This task requires real Linux and macOS execution environments; do not claim completion from win32 alone.
Use production @moe/runner/platform and distribution/doctor surfaces, not test reimplementations.
Every refusal/unknown asserts stable code plus layer/boundary and every generated schedule asserts positive cardinality.

comments.content:
GOVERNOR — CI RUNNER AUTHORED. TASK STAYS BLOCKED. Read before claiming: the gap is narrower now but NOT closed.

Human instructed the governor to land small fixes directly. I wrote `.github/workflows/cross-host.yml` (55 lines, new file, `.github/` did not exist before). It is COMMITTED TO THE WORKING TREE ONLY — NOT pushed. No CI run exists yet.

WHAT IT CLOSES. CAUSE 2 of this block reads "no Linux or macOS runner exists to delegate to" and lists `.github/`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `azure-pipelines.yml`, `.circleci` as all absent. `.github/workflows/cross-host.yml` now exists: a `gate` job over `matrix.os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest]`, triggered on push to any branch, on pull_request, and on workflow_dispatch. `fail-fast: false` deliberately — a red Linux leg must not cancel the macOS leg, because the wanted evidence is PER HOST and a cancelled leg is UNKNOWN, not a result. Steps: checkout, record host facts (`runner.os`, `uname -a`), pnpm 11.0.8 via pnpm/action-setup@v4, Node 24.16.0 via actions/setup-node@v4 with pnpm cache, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, a platform-identity probe printing `{platform, arch, node}`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`. Versions taken from the repo's own manifest (`packageManager: pnpm@11.0.8`, `engines.node: >=24.16.0 <25`), not guessed.

WHAT IT DOES NOT CLOSE, AND WHY THIS TASK STAYS BLOCKED:
1. A workflow FILE is not an execution. DoD 1 wants PROVEN/UNKNOWN against the production classifier on real hosts. That needs a RUN, and a run needs a push to `origin git@github.com:yaront1111/Moe-NG.git`. Pushing triggers CI on the human's account, so it is theirs to authorize, not mine.
2. `tests/fault/linux` and `tests/fault/macos` are still ABSENT on disk. Even a green run proves the suites that exist today pass on Linux and macOS; it does not produce the per-boundary host evidence this task's DoD names. Someone still has to author those tests.
3. HONEST LIMIT ON MY VERIFICATION: my first YAML parse of this file failed with a precise scanner error (line 49, col 47 — an unquoted scalar containing `: `), which I fixed by moving that command under a block scalar. My attempt to RE-PARSE after the fix was blocked by the environment, so the file has been read end to end by eye but has NOT been re-parsed clean. Treat "valid YAML" as unconfirmed until a run or a local parse says otherwise. The first red flag it throws will be a syntax error, not a silent wrong result.

UNBLOCK SEQUENCE FROM HERE: human pushes -> a real Linux and macOS run exists -> author the per-boundary host evidence under tests/fault/{linux,macos} -> re-measure -> flip to PLANNING. Note CAUSE 1 of the original block died earlier today: task-45d12ecf is DONE, `packages/runner/src/platform/macos/` exists, `PLATFORM_MACOS` is in the contract.

DOWNSTREAM: this task also gates task-22cfca91 (Portability shadow gate), whose other five of seven prerequisites are already DONE, and part of task-05ce9b8f (Security fault matrix). One push is worth more than one ticket.
